summary.text: The Battle of the Somme was a First World War battle fought from 1 July to 18 November 1916 in France by British and French armies against the German Empire.
More than three million men fought, and more than one million were wounded or killed, making it one of the deadliest battles in human history.
The Allies pushed 6.2 miles (10 km) into German-occupied territory along most of the front, but did not achieve their operational objectives.

facts.label: Men who fought
facts.value: More than three million, with over one million wounded or killed

facts.label: First day
facts.value: 57,470 British casualties, the worst in British Army history

facts.label: New technology
facts.value: The first use of the tank, in September

facts.label: Ground gained
facts.value: British and French forces advanced 6.2 miles (10 km)

items.prompt: Germany attacks at Verdun in February 1916, drawing in French divisions meant for another offensive. How does this change the planned Somme attack?

options.label: The French take over the whole offensive
The British attack becomes the main effort
The offensive is cancelled for the year
The Russians carry the main attack

items.explain: French commanders diverted divisions to Verdun, so the supporting British attack became the principal effort.

items.prompt: By 31 May 1916 a grand plan for a decisive victory has shrunk. What is the Somme offensive now meant to do?

options.label: Capture Berlin before the winter of 1916
Drive the Germans from the Belgian coast
End the war by splitting the German lines
Relieve pressure on the French and wear down German armies

items.explain: The plan was reduced to a limited offensive to relieve pressure at Verdun and inflict attrition on the German armies.

items.prompt: Falkenhayn attacks toward Verdun hoping to draw the French into a particular kind of fight. What was it?

options.label: An attrition battle where German terrain and firepower caused heavy French losses
A swift maneuver that trapped the French in open country
A naval clash that cut the French supply lines
A truce that split the French from the British

items.explain: He meant to induce the French to fight an attrition battle that would cost them disproportionate casualties.

items.prompt: Tanks and air power became notable at the Somme. How did these new technologies perform?

options.label: They were reliable and quickly decided the battle
They were left unused until the battle ended
They were important but proved unreliable, being products of new technology
They worked well only for the Germans

items.explain: The battle became notable for air power and the first tank use, but these were new technology and proved unreliable.

items.prompt: At the end of the battle, how did the Allied gains compare with their goals?

options.label: They captured every target and ended the stalemate
They gained their largest ground since 1914 but missed Péronne and Bapaume
They gained no ground at all along the front
They took Péronne and Bapaume but lost the rest

items.explain: The advance was their largest gain since the Marne, but the operational objectives, including Péronne and Bapaume, were not achieved.

items.prompt: British attacks in the Ancre valley continue into early 1917. What does Germany do in March 1917?

options.label: It retreats to the Hindenburg Line in a planned withdrawal
It launches a new offensive across the Somme
It holds Péronne and Bapaume until the summer
It hands the Somme region to the French

items.explain: Germany made a strategic retreat to the Siegfriedstellung (Hindenburg Line) in March 1917.
